images.title: A line of one half
images.purpose: Show that when the unit from 0 to 1 is cut into 2 equal gaps, a line covering the first gap is 1/2 unit long.
images.composition: One long horizontal number line across the middle of the frame with wide margins, and one thick line resting on it from 0 to the first mark.
images.exact_structure: A grey #6B7280 number line from 0 to 2 with exactly 5 evenly spaced ticks: 0, the mark halfway to 1, 1, the mark halfway to 2, and 2. The gap from 0 to 1 is exactly the same length as the gap from 1 to 2. A thick teal #0072B2 line runs from 0 to the first mark only. A thin amber #E69F00 bracket above 0 to 1 spans the two equal gaps. The tick for 1 is drawn in reddish purple #CC79A7. Exactly 1 number line, 1 teal line, 1 bracket.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
ticks that are not evenly spaced, or a teal line that reaches past the first mark
images.takeaway: Count the equal gaps from 0, not the marks.
images.description: A number line from 0 to 2 with each unit cut into 2 equal gaps; a teal line covers only the first gap and is labelled 1/2 unit, while a bracket shows 2 equal gaps make 1 unit.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the mark for 1 and count how many gaps the teal line covers before saying its length.

image_decisions.why: Reading a length by counting equal gaps from 0 is a picture idea; one clean number line carries it.
